newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Johnson Matthey profit boosts shares.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Johnson Matthey profit boosts shares.

text.p: British metals and electronic materials group Johnson Matthey Plc sent its shares surging on Thursday after it posted a six percent rise in annual profits and predicted further growth this year.
The company reported pretax profits of 108.3 million pounds ($176.9 million) for the year to March 31, nearing the top of analysts' forecasts, which ranged from 105 to 110 million pounds.

"We've achieved a six percent increase in profits while market conditions in three out of four of our divisions have been quite difficult," executive director Gordon Thorburn told Reuters in an interview.
The company's shares shot higher on the news, rising six percent, or 30 pence to 491.5 by 1000 GMT after opening near the 12-month low of 459 pence.
"The results are at the top end of forecasts, and that has lifted the shares," said one analyst.
Johnson Matthey, which makes about half of its profits in North America, expected profit growth this year to offset the impact of the pound's strength.
Thorburn predicted currency translation would trim annual profits by about 1.5 million pounds, roughly the same level as last year.
Worries over the pound's impact have depressed Johnson Matthey shares earlier this year.
"The outlook is good. We're expecting very strong growth in our Electronic Materials division and a further rise in the Catalytic Systems division," he said.
In addition, higher prices should help the Precious Metals division, which accounts for about 40 percent of the company's profits, he added.
"Since the end of March, precious metal prices have risen very substantially. That means we will make more money in that business," Thorburn said.
The division increased its operating profit by 4.0 percent to 44.0 million pounds last year despite weak precious metals prices.
But prices for platinum and palladium, used in car exhaust catalysts, have shot up this year.
Palladium hit its highest level in 17 years last week as Russian exports have halted.
The Electronics Materials unit should get a boost from the company's Plastic Land Grid Array (PLGA) technology as its new U.S. plant in Wisconsin comes fully onstream this year.
The company expected to reach full capacity production of about 1.5 million units per month toward the end of its financial year in March.
Thorburn also said a new cross-licensing pact with Japan's Kyocera Corp would help business.

Under the deal, Johnson Matthey will license to Kyocera its PLGA technology, while the Japanese firm will license its technology for future generations of plastic laminate packages for semiconductors.
"(The agreement) is worth a very great deal, but the commercial details are confidential," Thorburn said.
Profits in the Electronic Materials division grew 21 percent to 30.9 million pounds, while Catalytic Systems profits rose 30 percent to 34.1 million pounds.
But fell at Johnson Matthey's ceramics venture with Cookson Group Plc, hit by low sales prices and weak demand in the European tile market.
Cookson Matthey Ceramics' profits dropped 36 percent to 15.3 million pounds for the year.

"The strategic development of Johnson Matthey as a leading global company in advanced materials technology remains on track, and we expect further milestones to be achieved during the coming year," the company said.
($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
